title: Semiconductor basics: carriers, doping and junctions
summary: Build a working model of conductors, insulators, doped silicon and the depletion region before selecting any device.

blocks.title: Why silicon can act like a switch
blocks.body: A machinist controls motion by changing geometry and force. Semiconductor devices control current by changing which charge carriers can move and where. This lesson builds that model without pretending a band diagram is a wiring instruction.

columns.name: Conductor
columns.detail: Many mobile carriers make current relatively easy to establish. Resistance still depends on material, dimensions and temperature.

columns.name: Insulator
columns.detail: Very few carriers are available under normal conditions, so current is strongly limited until an electrical or physical limit is exceeded.

columns.name: Semiconductor
columns.detail: Its carrier population and conductivity can be engineered with doping, fields, light and temperature. “Semiconductor” does not mean a fixed resistance halfway between copper and glass.

blocks.heading: 2. Doping sets majority carriers
blocks.body: Pure silicon has four valence electrons per atom. Adding controlled donor impurities contributes electrons, producing n-type material whose majority carriers are electrons. Acceptor impurities create holes, producing p-type material whose majority carriers are holes. Both types remain electrically neutral overall; n-type does not mean a negatively charged block, and p-type does not mean a positively charged block.

blocks.heading: 3. Form a p-n junction
items: When p-type and n-type material meet, carriers diffuse across the boundary and recombine.
Fixed ionized dopants remain near the boundary. This space-charge region has few mobile carriers and is called the depletion region.
Its internal electric field opposes further diffusion, establishing a built-in barrier at equilibrium.
External bias changes that barrier. Forward bias lowers it and reverse bias raises it, which is the basis for diode behavior.

blocks.heading: 4. Check the model
options: The whole piece carries a permanent negative charge.
Electrons are the majority carriers because donor dopants were added.
blocks.explanation: Doping changes the balance of mobile carriers, not the overall electrical neutrality of the material.

items.label: Label the carriers
items.detail: Write the majority carrier for n-type and p-type material.

items.label: Describe the junction
items.detail: In one sentence each, explain diffusion, recombination and the depletion region.

items.label: Predict the bias effect
items.detail: State whether forward bias makes the junction barrier easier or harder for carriers to cross.

items.label: Name a limit
items.detail: Write why this model alone cannot select a real diode, transistor or rating.
